## Exact code to write

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware   # re-exported from starlette

app = FastAPI()

# ── Allowed origins ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# http://localhost:3000  → typical Create-React-App / Next.js dev server
# http://localhost:5173  → typical Vite (React / Vue / Svelte) dev server
origins = [
    "http://localhost:3000",
    "http://localhost:5173",
]

# ── CORS middleware ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Must be added BEFORE any route definitions so the middleware wraps every
# request/response that passes through the application.
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=origins,       # exact list of permitted origins
    allow_credentials=True,      # allow cookies / Authorization headers
    allow_methods=["*"],         # GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS, …
    allow_headers=["*"],         # Content-Type, Authorization, X-*, …
)


@app.get("/")
async def main():
    return {"message": "Hello World"}
```

## Line-by-line explanation

| Code | Why |
|---|---|
| `from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware` | `fastapi/middleware/cors.py` is a thin re-export of `starlette.middleware.cors.CORSMiddleware`; always use the FastAPI path so it stays consistent with the rest of the framework |
| `origins = [...]` | A plain list of **exact** origin strings. CORS matching is case-sensitive and protocol-sensitive — `http://` and `https://` are different origins |
| `app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, ...)` | Starlette wraps middleware in LIFO order; calling this before any route decorators guarantees the CORS headers are injected on every response, including validation-error responses |
| `allow_credentials=True` | Needed when the frontend sends `fetch(..., { credentials: 'include' })` or uses `axios` with `withCredentials: true` (cookies, HTTP auth). **If you set this, `allow_origins` must be an explicit list — `["*"]` is rejected by browsers when credentials are included** |
| `allow_methods=["*"]` | Permits all HTTP verbs in pre-flight (`OPTIONS`) responses |
| `allow_headers=["*"]` | Permits any request header (e.g. `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, custom `X-*` headers) |

> **Production tip:** Replace the `origins` list with your real production domain(s) before deploying. Never ship `["*"]` as `allow_origins` together with `allow_credentials=True` — browsers will block it, and it would be a security hole if they didn't.
